features.name: All-in price toggle
features.description: A results-page control that recalculates every fare and list price to include a typical carry-on and seat so shown prices reflect what a normal traveler actually pays.
features.hmw: How might we help a traveler see the price they will actually pay before they commit to a fare?

features.name: One-time traveler profile
features.description: The traveler states baggage, seat, and flexibility needs once and the system marks which fare class is cheapest for them, removing the need to decode the fare panel.
features.hmw: How might we help a traveler see the price they will actually pay before they commit to a fare?

features.name: Running trip-cost card
features.description: A persistent breakdown of fare plus seat, bags, and fees that stays visible from results through checkout and updates as choices change.
features.hmw: How might we help a traveler see the price they will actually pay before they commit to a fare?

features.name: Price-first default sort
features.description: Change the default results sort from Recommended to Price low-to-high, with the previous sort one tap away.
features.hmw: How might we surface the choices that most affect price so a traveler does not miss them by accepting the defaults?

features.name: Cheaper-nearby-date nudge
features.description: An inline banner on results when a date within a few days is materially cheaper, showing the price delta.
features.hmw: How might we surface the choices that most affect price so a traveler does not miss them by accepting the defaults?

features.name: Inline what's-included strip
features.description: Move the fare-structure disclosure out of the sidebar onto every result card as a compact carry-on / seat / change-fee strip.
features.hmw: How might we surface the choices that most affect price so a traveler does not miss them by accepting the defaults?

features.name: Single pricing source of truth
features.description: One service computes every price shown on the fare panel, bags page, and checkout so bag and fee figures can never disagree between screens.
features.hmw: How might we keep cost information consistent and trustworthy as a traveler moves through the booking?

features.name: Fix 'Continue without bags?' copy
features.description: Make the confirmation dialog reflect actual cart contents, including the carry-on that is already included, instead of a hardcoded incorrect string.
features.hmw: How might we keep cost information consistent and trustworthy as a traveler moves through the booking?

features.name: Mixed-carrier risk flag
features.description: When a selection would combine two airlines, show a plain-language note about separate rebooking and delay liability before the option is added.
features.hmw: How might we let a traveler weigh a cheaper option against its trade-offs, such as a split-airline itinerary?

features.name: Return options shown as totals
features.description: Display the full itinerary total on each return option with the delta kept as a smaller secondary number.
features.hmw: How might we let a traveler weigh a cheaper option against its trade-offs, such as a split-airline itinerary?

features.name: Symmetric accept/decline controls
features.description: Render decline and accept as equal-weight controls on interstitials, insurance, and SMS opt-in, with no pre-checked boxes.
features.hmw: How might we give a traveler a clear, pressure-free way to decline add-ons they do not want?

features.name: Neutral decline language
features.description: Replace the self-incriminating insurance decline copy with a factual statement of the choice, shown alongside the 24-hour free-cancellation fact.
features.hmw: How might we give a traveler a clear, pressure-free way to decline add-ons they do not want?

design_directions.name: The number is the number
design_directions.summary: Bet that the core failure is the displayed price itself: make every price shown, from the first results screen onward, an all-in figure that already includes what a typical traveler buys, with the system assembling that realistic bundle rather than the user.
design_directions.differentiator: No price anywhere in the flow excludes carry-on and seat by default; the headline figure and the paid figure are the same number.
hmws_addressed: How might we help a traveler see the price they will actually pay before they commit to a fare?
How might we surface the choices that most affect price so a traveler does not miss them by accepting the defaults?
How might we keep cost information consistent and trustworthy as a traveler moves through the booking?
design_directions.tradeoff: All-in prices look higher than competitors' headline fares, which can hurt comparison-shopping conversion, and travelers who genuinely want the bare a la carte fare lose the stripped-down view.

design_directions.name: Guided fare coach
design_directions.summary: Bet that travelers cannot be expected to decode fare structure at all: ask a few questions up front about bags, seat, and flexibility, then steer the traveler to the right fare class and date and collapse the fare-panel decision into a recommendation.
design_directions.differentiator: The product makes the fare-class and date call on the traveler's behalf instead of presenting options for them to compare.
hmws_addressed: How might we help a traveler see the price they will actually pay before they commit to a fare?
How might we surface the choices that most affect price so a traveler does not miss them by accepting the defaults?
How might we let a traveler weigh a cheaper option against its trade-offs, such as a split-airline itinerary?
design_directions.tradeoff: Adds an upfront questioning step, the fare-structure scrutinizer feels railroaded and distrusts a flow that decides for them, and any wrong recommendation damages trust more than a confusing menu would.

design_directions.name: Honest broker checkout
design_directions.summary: Bet that the damage is concentrated in the back half of the flow: leave search and results mostly alone and rebuild fare selection through checkout around consistent totals, symmetric accept/decline choices, and explicit trade-off disclosure.
design_directions.differentiator: Scope is deliberately limited to the decision and confirmation steps; discovery is treated as good enough and left untouched.
hmws_addressed: How might we keep cost information consistent and trustworthy as a traveler moves through the booking?
How might we let a traveler weigh a cheaper option against its trade-offs, such as a split-airline itinerary?
How might we give a traveler a clear, pressure-free way to decline add-ons they do not want?
design_directions.tradeoff: Does nothing for the traveler who overpays at the results stage by keeping the default date and sort, so it leaves the two highest-severity themes only partly addressed.
